question: In quadrilateral PQRS, the bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at the point T (inside the quadrilateral) and ∠STR = 14°. If the ratio of ∠P to ∠Q is 2 : 5, then what is the difference between the measures of ∠Q and ∠P?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In any quadrilateral, the angle formed by the intersection of bisectors of two adjacent angles equals half the sum of the remaining two angles.

⇒ ∠STR = (∠P + ∠Q) ÷ 2

⇒ 14° = (∠P + ∠Q) ÷ 2 ⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 28°

Given ∠P : ∠Q = 2 : 5, total ratio parts = 2 + 5 = 7.

Difference in parts = 5 − 2 = 3 parts.

⇒ Difference = (3 ÷ 7) × 28° = 12°

**∴ The correct answer is 12°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Angle bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at point T.

⇒ ∠STR = 14°

⇒ Ratio of ∠P : ∠Q = 2 : 5

**Calculations:**

⇒ In ΔSTR, the sum of interior angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠TSR + ∠TRS + ∠STR = 180°

⇒ Since ST and RT are angle bisectors, ∠TSR = ∠S ÷ 2 and ∠TRS = ∠R ÷ 2

⇒ (∠S ÷ 2) + (∠R ÷ 2) + 14° = 180°

⇒ (∠S + ∠R) ÷ 2 = 180° − 14° = 166°

⇒ ∠S + ∠R = 166° × 2 = 332°

⇒ We know the sum of all angles in quadrilateral PQRS is 360°.

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q + ∠R + ∠S = 360°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q + 332° = 360°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 28°

⇒ Let the measures of ∠P and ∠Q be 2x and 5x respectively.

⇒ 2x + 5x = 28°

⇒ 7x = 28° ⇒ x = 4°

⇒ Difference between ∠Q and ∠P = 5x − 2x = 3x

⇒ 3 × 4° = 12°

**∴ The correct answer is 12°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all interior angles of any n-sided polygon is given by the formula (n − 2) × 180°. For a quadrilateral (n = 4), the sum is exactly 360°.

Angle Bisector Property in Quadrilaterals

The angle formed by the bisectors of any two adjacent angles of a quadrilateral is equal to half the sum of the other two angles: ∠AOB = (∠C + ∠D) ÷ 2.

Cyclic Quadrilateral

A quadrilateral whose all four vertices lie on a single circle is a cyclic quadrilateral. The opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are always supplementary (sum up to 180°).
